readings: a premium economy seat is a preferred seat (a seat bought at additional cost for more legroom), reimbursed with the supervisor's approval up to the lesser of 10% of the airfare or $100
premium economy is a higher class than coach, so it is an upgrade the University does not pay; the preferred-seat rule covers seat fees within the same class

request: Could you book me premium economy on the American flight to Charlotte on Tuesday, December 15? My supervisor has approved a preferred seat for this trip. I'd rather not pay anything extra myself.

must_keep.quote: V. Preferred Seating - Seats for purchase on an aircraft at an additional cost. Some of the benefits preferred seating may provide are more legroom, priority boarding and/or early access to overhead bins.
must_keep.why: definition V: preferred seating, seats bought at extra cost, e.g. more legroom

must_keep.quote: When in the best interest of the University, the supervisor (or his/her designee) or the person with fiscal responsibility unless the Campus and/or Department requires a higher level of approval may approve reimbursement of the purchase of a preferred seat. The fee for the preferred seat will be reimbursed at the lesser of 10% of the airfare or up to $100.
must_keep.why: a preferred seat, approved by the supervisor, at the lesser of 10% of the airfare or $100

must_keep.quote: Commercial air travel will not be reimbursed more than lowest logical coach/economy class rates when it has been determined to be the best value. The difference between coach/economy class rates and first class or business class rates will be paid by the traveler.
must_keep.why: the University pays the lowest logical coach fare; the traveller pays any difference

must_keep.quote: Upgrades at the expense of the University are not permitted unless there is a medical accommodation on file with the Office of Civil Rights & Title IX for employees, Office of the Dean of Students Disability Services for students, or documentation from the contracted travel agency indicating the higher-class ticket is the lowest priced airfare available.
must_keep.why: no upgrade at University expense, with three exceptions

must_keep.quote: This permanent memorandum allows for discretion or exceptions approved by the President of the University or his/her designee.
must_keep.why: who may settle a discretionary question

design_notes: Premium economy is 5500 cents above coach on the same flight (8.6%, under both 10% of the airfare and $100), and a preferred-seat approval is on file. If a premium economy seat is a "preferred seat" (definition V: a seat bought at extra cost, e.g. for legroom), the University reimburses it (lines 429-433); if it is a higher class, it is an upgrade at University expense, not permitted (lines 399-405). Hold.
